answer: An optical challenge protocol curbs Sybil attacks by anchoring agent identities to dedicated photonic hardware. Verifiers pulse saffron light toward a candidate's micro-electromechanical mirror, measuring the phase and return echo to verify a discrete physical resonator. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating and powering separate optoelectronic chips per identity. However, ambient thermal expansion causes phase drift, occasionally rejecting legitimate agents.
